\chapter{Likely or not}
\label{ch:ar-likely-or-not}
\hlchaptermodality{401}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can talk about a probability, say what is probable, and say that something is likely or ruled out.}

Complete the last lesson of chapter 401: I can talk about a probability, say what is probable, and say that something is likely or ruled out.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{احتمال} (iḥtimāl)}{احتمال (iḥtimāl)}]{\ar{احتمال} (iḥtimāl) — a probability}

\label{lesson:AR-C401-ihtimal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for whether, then the Arabic for wherever.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{احتمال}}
\textbf{\ar{احتمال}} — \emph{iḥtimāl} — \textquotedblleft{}a probability\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{هناك} \ar{احتمال} \ar{كبير} \ar{للمطر} \ar{غدا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hunāka iḥtimāl kabīr li-l-maṭar ghadan.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There is a high probability of rain tomorrow.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{احتمال}} (\emph{iḥtimāl}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-m-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to carry, to bear\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Iḥtimāl} is the Form VIII verbal noun, bearing a thing, allowing for it: a probability.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iḥtimāl}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iḥtimāl}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hunāka iḥtimāl kabīr li-l-maṭar ghadan.} — There is a high probability of rain tomorrow.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for whether, then the Arabic for wherever, then say \emph{iḥtimāl} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{احتمال} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A probability\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{محتمل} (muḥtamal)}{محتمل (muḥtamal)}]{\ar{محتمل} (muḥtamal) — probable}

\label{lesson:AR-C401-muhtamal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for wherever, then the Arabic for a probability.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{محتمل}}
\textbf{\ar{محتمل}} — \emph{muḥtamal} — \textquotedblleft{}probable\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{من} \ar{المحتمل} \ar{أن} \ar{يتأخر} \ar{أخي}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{min al-muḥtamal an yataʾakhkhara akhī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
It is probable that my brother will be late.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{محتمل}} (\emph{muḥtamal}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-m-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to carry, to bear\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Muḥtamal} is the Form VIII passive participle: what can be allowed for, probable.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muḥtamal}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muḥtamal}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{min al-muḥtamal an yataʾakhkhara akhī.} — It is probable that my brother will be late.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for wherever, then the Arabic for a probability, then say \emph{muḥtamal} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{محتمل} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Probable\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{احتمل} (iḥtamala)}{احتمل (iḥtamala)}]{\ar{احتمل} (iḥtamala) — to tolerate; to allow for}

\label{lesson:AR-C401-ihtamala}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a probability, then the Arabic for probable.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{احتمل}}
\textbf{\ar{احتمل}} — \emph{iḥtamala} — \textquotedblleft{}to tolerate; to allow for\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{لا} \ar{يحتمل} \ar{جدي} \ar{الحر}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{lā yaḥtamilu jaddī al-ḥarr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My grandfather cannot tolerate the heat.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يحتمل}, \emph{yaḥtamil}.

\ar{يحتمل} \ar{أن} …, it is possible that ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{احتمل}} (\emph{iḥtamala}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-m-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to carry, to bear\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form VIII, to carry a load oneself: to bear, to tolerate, and so to allow for a thing.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iḥtamala}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iḥtamala}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lā yaḥtamilu jaddī al-ḥarr.} — My grandfather cannot tolerate the heat.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a probability, then the Arabic for probable, then say \emph{iḥtamala} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{احتمل} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To tolerate; to allow for\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{رجح} (rajjaḥa)}{رجح (rajjaḥa)}]{\ar{رجح} (rajjaḥa) — to consider likely}

\label{lesson:AR-C401-rajjaha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for probable, then the Arabic for to tolerate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{رجح}}
\textbf{\ar{رجح}} — \emph{rajjaḥa} — \textquotedblleft{}to consider likely\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{يرجح} \ar{الأطباء} \ar{أن} \ar{السبب} \ar{هو} \ar{التوتر}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yurajjiḥu al-aṭibbāʾ anna as-sabab huwa at-tawattur.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Doctors consider it likely that the cause is stress.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يرجح}, \emph{yurajjiḥ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{رجح}} (\emph{rajjaḥa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-j-ḥ}, \textquotedblleft{}to outweigh (of a scale)\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form II, to make one pan of the scale outweigh the other: to judge a thing more likely.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rajjaḥa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rajjaḥa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yurajjiḥu al-aṭibbāʾ anna as-sabab huwa at-tawattur.} — Doctors consider it likely that the cause is stress.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for probable, then the Arabic for to tolerate, then say \emph{rajjaḥa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{رجح} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To consider likely\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{استبعد} (istabʿada)}{استبعد (istabʿada)}]{\ar{استبعد} (istabʿada) — to rule out}

\label{lesson:AR-C401-istabada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to tolerate, then the Arabic for to consider likely.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{استبعد}}
\textbf{\ar{استبعد}} — \emph{istabʿada} — \textquotedblleft{}to rule out\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{استبعد} \ar{المدير} \ar{هذا} \ar{الاحتمال}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{istabʿada al-mudīr hādhā al-iḥtimāl.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The manager ruled out this possibility.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يستبعد}, \emph{yastabʿid}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{استبعد}} (\emph{istabʿada}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{b-ʿ-d}, \textquotedblleft{}to be far\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form X, to hold a thing to be far off: to rule it out. \ar{بعيد}, far, is from the same root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istabʿada}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istabʿada}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istabʿada al-mudīr hādhā al-iḥtimāl.} — The manager ruled out this possibility.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to tolerate, then the Arabic for to consider likely, then say \emph{istabʿada} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{استبعد} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To rule out\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
